label: Labels On A Phone Stop Cutting Themselves Short
desc: A stat cell in the admin user panel printed "SESSIO..." because four cells were sharing a row that only fits two, and the same mistake was made in about thirty other places: the ellipsis is meant for a URL or an email address, which can be any length, and it had been pointed at labels we wrote ourselves. An admin panel's own heading clipped to "Look Up Any H...", the scan summary's SSL cell read "SSL G...", every check title on /checks was cut roughly in half on a phone, and two API endpoints in the playground could clip to the same visible text. Those containers are now sized to fit the words they hold, because we already know what the words are: stat cells sit two per row on a phone, panel headings take their own line above the buttons, and titles wrap instead of being trimmed. Only genuinely unbounded values still clip, and more of them now carry the full text as a tooltip.

label: Rows Stop Crushing Their Own Contents On A Phone
desc: A row that keeps its buttons on the right at every screen width gives them what they need and leaves the value whatever is left. On a 320px screen that meant a verified domain had about zero pixels for the domain name, a webhook showed roughly ten characters of its endpoint, and a blocked-URL rule showed about seventy pixels of a full URL. Those rows now stack on a phone and go back to one line from tablet width up: domains, webhooks, blocked URLs and IP rules, the email log, backup files, staff invites, the Stripe event list, the repo page header and the share-link copy box. The browser session's network log drops its resource-type column on a phone so the request path has room, the gift-subscription form is one column so its date field is not clipped by the picker, and the daily-quota table in the rate-limit docs sits two across instead of squeezing four.

label: Controls You Can Hit With A Thumb
desc: The notifications bell, the tour's pause button, the browser session's extend-time button, the subdomain list's open and scan controls, and the edit and delete buttons on the admin notification, team, IP-rule, broadcast, domain, webhook and schedule rows were all drawn at between 12 and 32 pixels, which is fine with a mouse and awkward with a finger. Each one keeps the icon exactly the size it was and grows only the area you can press, back to the desktop size from tablet width up.

label: Long IDs Stop Pushing The Page Sideways
desc: A session id, a user id, an IPv6 address, a cookie id and an updater job id are each one unbroken run of characters, and printed with nowhere to break they set the width of whatever they sat in and made the whole page scroll sideways. They wrap now. The admin lookup panel does the same with whatever URL was pasted into it, and a repository description reads as two lines of prose rather than one clipped line.

label: Finding Names Are Printed In Full, Not Cut To Four Words
desc: A check title is one of our own, out of the catalogue, so anywhere one is listed the row can simply be sized to hold it. Three places had it clipped instead: the dashboard's "Most common findings" ranking, where the numbering and the count column left about 185px for a name like "Missing Content-Security-Policy header" that needs 260; the per-page finding list under a crawl, indented and carrying a severity word; and the compare view, whose entire job is telling you which findings differ between two scans. They wrap onto a second line now. The scan progress checklist does the same with its check-family names, the billing panel with your plan name, and the chat's slash-command list with the sentence describing each command, which was being cut after about four words at every window size.

label: The Hosts Page Stat Strip Fits On A Phone
desc: /assets is the only three-cell stat strip in the app, and three cells was the one count laid out the same way at every width. On a 390px screen that gave each cell about 119px, and after the padding and the icon roughly 43px of text: "EXPLOITABLE" needs about 74 and a four-digit count about 67, so both the caption and the number were clipped. The three cells stack on a phone and go back to a row from tablet width up, and the loading placeholder now matches, as does the scan summary's placeholder, which was drawing three readouts to a line where the real strip draws two.

label: More Controls You Can Actually Hit
desc: The back arrow out of an admin user's detail panel, the edit and delete buttons on an admin note, the delete button on a badge, the rename pencil on a team, the close button on the team invite form, and both dismiss controls on the cookie bar that sits over the bottom of every page were drawn between 24 and 32 pixels. They are 44 on a phone and back to their old size from tablet width up. Three controls that live inside a text field and so cannot grow (the finding search's clear button, the /checks filter's, and the browser session's close-panel button) keep their size and widen only the area that answers a thumb.

label: A Backup Code Is Never Shown Half-Printed
desc: The two-factor backup codes are shown exactly once, and they were rendered in a box that would clip a code with an ellipsis rather than report that it did not fit. Copying still worked, but what you wrote down would have been wrong. A code that does not fit now wraps instead.
